meta.dataset: Fair Harbor (Broad Sky Partners portfolio) - public filings and financial research track

subject.company: Fair Harbor Clothing PBC (f/k/a Fair Harbor Clothing Inc.), Delaware; operating HQ 520 Broadway, New York NY
subject.sponsor: Broad Sky Partners (Fund I, $335M); deal lead Jonathan Marlow

meta.scope_note: Part of the portfolio-wide filings track (all BSP portfolio companies and their rivals). Chubbies (Solo Brands) is included here as the closest public rival benchmark; similar-site peers from Similarweb are Maui and Sons, Vilebrequin, Kenny Flowers and Funky Trunks.
meta.method: SEC EDGAR full-text search and submissions API (Fair Harbor, Danehy, Broad Sky Partners, Mazzucchelli, Chubbies); EDGAR Form D XML; USAspending.gov award API for SBA PPP/EIDL; NY DOS Public Inquiry API; USPTO tmsearch backend query on owner name; Fair Harbor Shopify products.json/collections.json; Wayback Machine CDX and snapshots for Business Wire, WWD, Inc., B Lab, PitchBook and company pages; CourtListener v4 search API; Similarweb public pages via WebFetch; Solo Brands 10-K text. The WebSearch budget was exhausted before this track began, so discovery relied on direct endpoints and Wayback indexes rather than search engines.
meta.sources_summary: 13 distinct primary or near-primary sources: SEC EDGAR (Form D x2, VTEX 20-F, Solo Brands 10-Ks), USAspending/SBA, NY DOS, USPTO, B Lab, Inc., Business Wire, WWD, PitchBook, CourtListener, Similarweb, the company Shopify storefront, and the Broad Sky website.
caveats: No revenue, EBITDA or debt figure for Fair Harbor has been disclosed publicly; every financial estimate here is inferred.
Inc. 5000 revenue was not shown on the archived profile; the 2020 revenue range is derived from the 11,475% growth rate and Inc's $100K minimum base-year revenue.
PPP jobs-reported, lender and forgiveness fields are not in USAspending; ProPublica and FederalPay returned bot checks or 403s and were not bypassed.
Similarweb public figures are modeled estimates and understate absolute traffic; only the Fair Harbor-to-Chubbies ratio is used, and with low confidence.
Caroline's surname is misspelled 'Danehey' on the Form D; Jake Danehy signed it as President and CEO.
The Form D shows 24 investors and $30.7M sold but not Broad Sky's ownership percentage; enterprise value is a wide range because of this.
Bankruptcy-docket hits (FH-20) are text matches only; Fair Harbor's role and any claim amounts are unverified.

Funded-debt note from verification: USPTO assignment records show ABL security interests on the core mark from Merchant Financial (2020-2021) and Gerber Finance/eCapital (2021-2025, released 2025-12-11), so the 'no agent-bank lien confirmed' gap and the Funded debt estimate should be read in that light.
meta.financial_picture: 1) Fair Harbor was bootstrapped from about $24K of first-year sales (2015) and a projected $250K in 2017 to an Inc. 5000 #26 ranking with 11,475% three-year growth, so 2020 revenue was about 116x the 2017 base. That puts 2020 revenue at no less than about $11.6M, and plausibly $17-29M if the 2017 base was $150-250K. 2) Headcount and payroll were tiny: a $16,994 PPP loan implies about $82K of annualized W-2 payroll, and Inc listed 1-10 employees, so the pre-deal model was highly outsourced and founder-run. 3) The Broad Sky deal (March 2022) was Fair Harbor's first institutional capital: $30.73M of primary equity sold to 24 investors (Form D), with $6.0M more authorized. At about 9% of Broad Sky's $335M Fund I, this was a platform-sized check. 4) Broad Sky's ownership share is not disclosed. If Broad Sky holds a control stake of 60-80% with light leverage, the implied enterprise value is about $40-90M, or roughly 1.3-2.5x an estimated 2021 revenue of $30-40M. That is below the Chubbies precedent (~$130M, Sept 2021) but fits a brand about a quarter of Chubbies' size. 5) No BDC schedule-of-investments line, lender press release, credit rating or Form D for a debt vehicle mentions Fair Harbor. The capital structure is likely equity-heavy with at most an asset-based revolver for inventory, not a sponsor-style unitranche. 6) The move of the core FAIR HARBOR trademark into Fair Harbor Clothing Topco LLC (Jersey City) fits a PE holdco structure and possibly a lender collateral package; the USPTO assignment record would confirm this. 7) After the deal, management spent capital on category breadth (fleece, flannels, denim, sweaters, polos, kids), two owned stores (SoHo; Palm Beach Gardens by February 2023), B Corp/PBC status (score 94.3) and women's swim. 8) Women's was paused and liquidated at about 70% off by December 2025, and 38.5% of live variants carried markdowns in September 2026. Both point to margin pressure and inventory clean-up in FY2025-FY2026. 9) Newer growth levers are licensing and partnerships (FootJoy, collegiate, HBO's White Lotus, Discovery, Rothy's, Athletic Brewing) and a B2B custom program. These are capital-light and wholesale-like, and they follow the path Chubbies took, where retail and wholesale reached 52% of 2025 sales. 10) Fair Harbor's web traffic is about 20% of Chubbies' (Similarweb, summer 2026). Scaled against Chubbies' $59M DTC, that suggests Fair Harbor web DTC of about $10-12M. With 35-45% wholesale, B2B and stores, total 2025 revenue is plausibly about $20-35M, meaning growth has been modest since 2021. 11) With Chubbies' segment economics as the ceiling (58-60% gross margin, 14-18% segment margin at $113-123M) and Fair Harbor's smaller scale, store leases and 2025 women's write-downs, Fair Harbor's EBITDA is likely low single-digit millions (about $0-4M). 12) At about 4.5 years into the hold with no exit, the likely exit is a strategic sale to a brand-management or outdoor/lifestyle acquirer, where the IP holdco structure and licensing momentum would support value.

Continued pandemic DTC growth ('grown significantly in the last two years'); cumulative 26M bottles at about 11 bottles per trunk is consistent with $60-80M cumulative sales through 2021
$30.7M equity at an assumed 60-80% stake plus light or no debt; cross-checked against the Chubbies $129.5M precedent at larger scale
Web traffic about 20% of Chubbies' multiplied by Chubbies DTC $59.1M gives about $10-12M web DTC, grossed up for 35-45% wholesale/B2B/stores; adjusted for the women's exit and heavy markdowns
Chubbies segment margin 14-18% at 4-5x the scale; Fair Harbor carries store leases, sub-scale overhead and FY2025 women's liquidation

estimate_table.estimate: No term loan or unitranche identified; likely an ABL/revolver under $10M
estimate_table.basis: No BDC schedule, lender press or rating found; Topco trademark assignment possibly tied to collateral
Typical for a $20-35M DTC apparel brand with 2 stores; not observed directly

data_gaps: BDC loan schedules (technique A): EDGAR full-text returned 0 hits for 'Fair Harbor' in 10-K/10-Q/N-CSR/N-PORT since 2022, and no lender 8-K or press release was found.
Credit ratings and private-credit press (technique E): none found or expected at this size; Debtwire and 9fin were not accessible.

PPP detail (technique B): jobs reported, lender and forgiveness were not retrieved. ProPublica and FederalPay blocked automated access and were not bypassed; the SBA FOIA CSV (about 100-200MB per file) was not downloaded.
UCC liens: the NY UCC system moved to ucc-efiling.dos.ny.gov and was not queried; Delaware UCC searches are fee-based. No agent-bank lien was confirmed.
Delaware entity records for Fair Harbor Clothing PBC and Fair Harbor Clothing Topco LLC (formation date, conversion to PBC) were not pulled because they are fee-based.
USPTO assignment reel/frame (the conveyance type for the Topco assignment and any security interest) was not retrieved because the assignment API was unreachable.

Trade press with revenue (Modern Retail, Glossy, Forbes 30 Under 30, Business of Fashion): the WebSearch budget was exhausted and Wayback CDX found no archived fair-harbor URLs on those domains, so no revenue quote was obtained.
Current door counts at Nordstrom, REI, Dick's, Huckberry and Scheels were not verified.
1% for the Planet membership was not verified (directory is JS-rendered).
Owned store count in 2026 was not verified (store-locator is JS-rendered).
OSHA/DOL WHD establishment searches were not performed; they are low relevance for an outsourced-manufacturing apparel brand.

Jonathan Marlow (Director - Broad Sky Partner, Consumer)

items.what_it_tells_us: This is the Broad Sky transaction: $30.7M of new equity sold to 24 accredited investors on 2022-03-15, with $6.0M of the $36.7M authorized still open (a second close, co-invest or rollover sleeve). No proceeds went to officers, so the filing covers only primary equity, not the founders' secondary. It is the only Form D Fair Harbor has filed, so the earlier seed and Kickstarter capital never needed an EDGAR notice.

items.title: Broad Sky Partners, LP Form D/A - fund size context for the Fair Harbor check
items.what_it_tells_us: Fund I closed at about $335M. A roughly $30M equity check in Fair Harbor would be about 9% of the fund, a normal platform-sized position for a $300M+ LMM fund. Fair Harbor was the fund's first consumer platform, completed about two months after Thomas Scientific in January 2022.

items.title: Business Wire: 'Fair Harbor Secures Investment from Broad Sky Partners'
items.what_it_tells_us: The release confirms a banker-run sell-side process (PwC Corporate Finance) and a DTC-first brand with a small wholesale base (Nordstrom, Saks, about 250 specialty doors). The stated uses were new product lines, retail channels and sustainability. At entry the brand was still mainly men's swim, with women's scheduled for April 2022.

items.title: WWD: 'Fair Harbor Gets Investment From Broad Sky Partners' (Jean E. Palmieri)

key_figures.plans: launch women's spring 2022; expand wholesale reach in 2022

items.what_it_tells_us: WWD independently confirms the channel picture in the release and adds no revenue figure. Trade press gave no revenue or valuation for the deal, which fits a private, undisclosed-terms transaction.

items.title: Inc. 5000 (2021): No. 26 overall, 11,475% three-year growth
items.filer_or_source_agency: Inc. magazine company profile (Wayback snapshots 2021-10-24 and 2022-06-16)

key_figures.regional_rank: Inc. 5000 Regionals: New York 2021, No. 4 (also industry rank 2, state rank 5, metro rank 6)

items.what_it_tells_us: 2020 revenue was about 116x 2017 revenue. Inc requires at least $100K of base-year revenue, so 2020 revenue was at least about $11.6M. With the company's own 2017 projection of about $250K as the base, 2020 would be about $29M. The '1-10 employees' figure points to a very lean W-2 headcount, with fulfilment and manufacturing outsourced.

items.title: Inc. early-stage profile: first-year sales and 2017 projection (data as of 2017-01-31)
items.what_it_tells_us: These numbers anchor the Inc growth math: about $24K in 2015, $100K+ in 2016, and a projected $250K in 2017. Applying the 115.75x Inc multiple to a 2017 base of $150K-$250K gives 2020 revenue of roughly $17-29M. The brand was bootstrapped on grant and Kickstarter money before Broad Sky.

items.title: Paycheck Protection Program loan (first draw)
items.what_it_tells_us: PPP loans were 2.5x average monthly payroll, so this implies only about $82K of annualized W-2 payroll in the base period, about 1-3 employees. It fits the Inc '1-10 employees' figure and shows a very asset-light, outsourced model through 2019-2020. No second-draw loan was found.

items.title: USPTO trademark portfolio - core registrations and category extensions (23 filings)
items.what_it_tells_us: The April 2020 and April 2021 filings were for a move into women's activewear, bags, towels and home. BREEZEKNIT, the patented-style liner brand, was registered in 2024. The company has filed no new marks since December 2021, so post-deal category expansion has used the existing FAIR HARBOR marks rather than new sub-brands.

items.title: USPTO: December 2021 'lifestyle platform' intent-to-use filings mostly abandoned
items.filed_or_dated: Filed 2021-12-03; dead (Refused/Dismissed) per TSDR: FAIR PEAKS 2023-03-30, other listed serials 2025-10-01
items.what_it_tells_us: Just before the Broad Sky close, management filed for a broad lifestyle and hospitality platform: home goods, a hotel and restaurant concept, a 'Fair Peaks' mountain line and a 'Fair Company' umbrella. Almost all of these lapsed, so the post-deal plan narrowed to apparel adjacencies. Only candles, water bottles and towels reached use. items.what_it_tells_us: The core IC25 mark was assigned outright to the Delaware Topco LLC in December 2025, the same day the eCapital (formerly Gerber Finance) ABL security interest was released. That pattern fits a refinancing or holdco restructuring in December 2025. The assignment record shows two earlier asset-based lenders against the mark (Merchant Financial 2020-2021; Gerber/eCapital 2021-2025), so the company used ABL facilities both before and after the Broad Sky deal. Any new lender's security interest is not recorded on this mark as of the TSDR pull. The Jersey City address is shared with the NY service-of-process address.

items.title: Certified B Corporation (B Lab) - overall B Impact Score 94.3

key_figures.legal_form: Delaware Public Benefit Corporation (Fair Harbor Clothing PBC)

items.what_it_tells_us: B Corp certification came three months after the Broad Sky close. The PBC conversion predates the deal: USPTO records show the name change from Fair Harbor Clothing Inc. to Fair Harbor Clothing PBC executed 2021-04-26. Certification matches Broad Sky's ESG thesis for the deal (Operating Partner Roberta Bowman). The bottle claim moved only from 26M to 27M between the releases, so it is not useful as a volume tracker.

items.title: Live Shopify catalog snapshot (products.json / collections.json)
items.what_it_tells_us: The brand has moved from swim only to a year-round men's lifestyle assortment: about 64% of SKUs are non-swim (tees, fleece, flannels, sweaters, denim, polos), plus a kids line. Pricing stays premium ($88 median). About 38% of variants carried a compare-at markdown at the end of the season, which points to meaningful promotional dependence. There are no women's products live.

items.title: Women's line paused and liquidated ('We're reworking our women's styles')

key_figures.status_dec_2025: collection withdrawn pending rework; remaining stock final sale

items.what_it_tells_us: Women's performance swim was a headline use of proceeds in 2022, and it was withdrawn about 3.5 years later with inventory cleared at around 70% off. That points to write-downs or margin drag in FY2025. The company is concentrating on men's and kids, and Chubbies moved the other way when it launched women's swim (Cheekies) in February 2026.

No acquisitions turned up, so Fair Harbor has grown organically as a platform with no add-ons.

items.title: Similarweb public traffic snapshot, August 2026 (Fair Harbor vs. Chubbies)
items.what_it_tells_us: Fair Harbor's web traffic is about 20% of Chubbies' in the same seasonal window. Applied to Chubbies' FY2025 DTC net sales of $59.1M, that implies roughly $10-12M of Fair Harbor web DTC. This is a very rough proxy: Chubbies DTC includes owned stores and marketplaces, and Similarweb's public counts understate absolute traffic for both sites. Fair Harbor's audience skews older (45-54) and male, with high engagement (6.3 pages per visit).

items.entity: Chubbies (Solo Brands segment) - closest public rival
items.title: Chubbies segment financials FY2024-FY2025 (Solo Brands 10-K)

key_figures.owned_stores_note: 7 store openings in 2024, 1 in 2025; eleven Chubbies retail stores operated

items.what_it_tells_us: This is the best public comp for Fair Harbor's economics: premium men's swim and lifestyle at about 58-60% gross margin, with segment EBITDA margin (as reported by Solo Brands) rising toward the mid-to-high teens at more than $100M of scale. Chubbies' growth now comes from wholesale partnerships, which are 52% of 2025 sales. Fair Harbor, at an estimated quarter of Chubbies' size, would carry proportionally heavier fixed costs, so its EBITDA margin is likely well below Chubbies' segment margin.

items.title: Chubbies acquisition price and debt funding (Sept 2021)
items.what_it_tells_us: This is a precedent for DTC men's swim and lifestyle brands at the 2021 valuation peak: about $130M for Chubbies, which was likely roughly 1-1.5x forward sales. Six months later, near the same peak, Broad Sky put about $30.7M of equity into Fair Harbor, which is consistent with a Fair Harbor enterprise value of perhaps $45-90M.
